html:
The Cascades Indians, or Watlala, were a Chinookan people who lived at the Cascades Rapids of the Columbia River, in the gorge between present Oregon and Washington.

The rapids were one of the great fishing and trading places of the Northwest. Boats had to be carried around them, which let the people who lived there control the river route and take tolls. Their kin downriver were the Chinook and Multnomah, and upriver the Wasco and Wishram. The Lewis and Clark Expedition passed them in 1805. Malaria epidemics in the 1830s killed most of them, and survivors joined the Yakama and Warm Springs reservations after the treaties of 1855.
